name: Test UI
blurb: Browse the project's proven-component kit — preview each component, read its API, see what it composes, and spot the gaps still to design. Optional; the UI stage is what commissions them.
prompt:
The Component Library pane is open for this project. It shows the proven-component kit(s) the app is
built from — for each component: a live preview, its variants, props/API, what it composes (and is
composed by), and its source. Use this stage to BROWSE: review which components the planned features
need, spot the gaps still to design, and get a feel for the kit's coverage.

This stage decides nothing. The UI stage owns the pipeline — it derives each screen's data shape,
queries the kit for that shape (`bsc ui shapes` / `bsc ui list --shape`), commissions the designer
for anything missing, pairs the app with a theme (`bsc plan ui set`), and bakes the kit's eslint
preset into the generated app. Do that work there, not here, so a project has ONE place its kit and
theme are settled.

Do NOT write component code in this stage — the designer authors components via `bsc ui`, and the
fleet builds against the kit later.
directive: **Test UI** — an OPTIONAL browsing surface over the project's proven-component kit: preview each component, read its API, see what it composes, and spot the gaps still to design. It is a reading stage and settles nothing. The **UI** stage owns the pipeline — shape derivation, the kit query (`bsc ui shapes` / `bsc ui list --shape`), commissioning the designer, the {kit, theme} pairing (`bsc plan ui set` → `bsc ui emit-css`) and baking the kit's eslint preset into the generated app all happen there, so a project has ONE place its kit and theme are settled (#4249 folded them out of here). Write no component code in this stage.
